db_evidence.notes: The true first-unlock event at 63367-63408s IS present in the DB and visually confirmed (boss kill at ~63360s -> shrine visit -> equipment menu -> 披挂铸造/Armament Forging screen open by 63377-63388s), matching the reference 'Forging, Armament Forging' almost exactly. However, none of the episode/visual_clips/event_steps/topic_facts captions in or near that 30-41s window mention 'fire-scorch', '火燎三关', 'Keeper's Shrine', or '土地庙' by name -- the captioner described only generic shrine-menu options (消息/领地/修行/铸造/货殖/赠礼/炼开/离开) without naming the stage or shrine. The only verbatim database hit for '火燎三关' is a single caption at 71100-71160s describing an unrelated, later pause/save-menu visit inside the fire-scorch stage itself (cursor on 存档). All 5 retrieval agents' semantic_search and run_sql calls converged on that single lexical match and never independently found or queried the 63367-63408 window, so the correct evidence was effectively unretrievable via the available search surface even though it exists in the DB.

root_causes: Lexical/embedding anchoring: the only caption containing the literal question keyword ('火燎三关') is a different, later, unrelated event; all 5 independent rollouts converged on it because semantic_search and manual run_sql time-window choices were driven by that keyword match rather than by the semantics of 'first unlocked ... at Keeper's Shrine'.

Caption/embedding gap at the true clue interval: the captioner never recorded the stage name, shrine name, or an 'unlock' notification text for the 63367-63408 window, so no keyword or semantic query phrased around the question's named entities (Fire-Scorch, Keeper's Shrine, 土地庙) could surface it.

No rollout tried a wider or earlier time search (e.g., scanning boss-kill/shrine-visit events well before 71000s) once the single '火燎三关' hit was found; all treated it as ground truth and jumped straight to clip_qa confirmation instead of validating that this was actually the FIRST unlock.

Question emphasizes 'first' unlocked, but no rollout looked for an earlier shrine visit/unlock notification predating the 71130s screen; they treated the only keyword match as automatically the first occurrence.
what_worked: clip_qa sub-agent visual reading was accurate and self-consistent for the frames it was given (correctly read 调息 as the top highlighted Chinese menu option each time) -- the visual sub-agent was not the source of error.
All 5 rollouts followed a similar disciplined skill-read -> semantic_search -> run_sql -> clip_qa -> submit pipeline, showing consistent tool usage.
transferable_lessons: For 'first X happened' questions, do not trust the single literal keyword match as the answer's location; explicitly search for and rule out earlier occurrences of the same entity/event before running clip_qa, e.g. run_sql over the full timeline for the named location/entity rather than only around the first semantic_search hit.

When a proper-noun/stage-name search returns exactly one hit, treat that as suspicious rather than confirmatory -- a single hit could be a caption that happens to mention the string while the actual first occurrence lacks that caption text (embedding/caption coverage gap).

Cross-check location identity before trusting the menu option: the reference implies the event is literally at 'Keeper's Shrine (土地庙)', but the 71130s screen's own caption describes a generic shrine encountered during boss-fight loot pickup in a lava/snow biome, not explicitly '土地庙'; verifying the location name visually (frame extraction) before committing would have flagged the mismatch.

Broaden the SQL/semantic_search time window substantially (or search around known anchor events like 'boss defeated' + 'menu opened' near shrines) instead of narrowly bracketing +/-150-350s around the sole keyword hit.
open_questions: Whether the memory database's captioning pipeline systematically drops game-specific UI/stage names for fast menu transitions (like the 2-3s cut into 披挂铸造 at 63367-63408), which would be a broader embeddings/captioning coverage gap affecting other similar 'first X' questions in this run.

Whether a differently-phrased semantic_search (e.g. searching for 'boss defeated near shrine then opens equipment/forging menu' instead of using the exact stage name) would have surfaced the 63367-63408 window; none of the 5 rollouts tried a location/action-based query decoupled from the literal stage name.
